A note that keeps growing past the point where a reader can hold it in one pass is no longer doing what a note is for, and the usual reason is that two arguments were welded together at the moment of writing, which is exactly the moment when the writer has the most context and the least distance, so the welding feels natural and is only visible later, when the note is read for a different purpose than the one it was written for, and at that point splitting it costs far more than it would have. ^[raw/articles/clean.md]
